title: Catch-All (Optional Parameter) Queries
description: A '(@p IS NULL OR col=@p)' catch-all gets one bad plan for every case; OPTION(RECOMPILE) folds the unused branches into a seek.
narrative:
## Scenario
A search screen lets the user optionally filter by customer. The classic "catch-all" pattern handles the optional filter in one query:

```sql
WHERE (@CustomerId IS NULL OR CustomerId = @CustomerId)
```

When `@CustomerId IS NULL` it should return everything; otherwise just that customer. But even when a value **is** supplied, the query scans the whole table.

## Why it's slow
SQL Server compiles **one** plan and caches it for reuse across all future values — including `@CustomerId IS NULL` (match everything). A plan that must be correct for the match-all case can't rely on seeking `CustomerId`, so the optimizer picks a **scan** that is safe for every value. The runtime value of `@CustomerId` doesn't change the cached plan.

## The fix
`OPTION (RECOMPILE)` tells SQL Server to recompile the statement **on each execution using the actual parameter value**. With `@CustomerId = 42`, the optimizer can prove the `@CustomerId IS NULL` branch is false, simplify the predicate to `CustomerId = 42`, and **seek** the index. The cost is a compile per execution — usually a fine trade for an otherwise unavoidable scan. (Building the statement as **dynamic SQL** with only the needed predicates is the other common fix.)

## Not the same as parameter sniffing
A separate lesson covers a *local variable* causing a cardinality **under-estimate**. Here the plan shape itself is forced wide by the `OR`-with-`NULL`; `RECOMPILE` fixes it by removing the branch at compile time.
hints: The (@p IS NULL OR col=@p) shape forces one plan that must also serve the match-all (@p IS NULL) case — a scan.
The runtime value can't change a cached plan. You need the optimizer to see the actual value at compile time.
Add OPTION (RECOMPILE) so the @CustomerId IS NULL branch is simplified away and CustomerId = @CustomerId can seek.
